channel_note: The official binary channel is the rolling prerelease tag series (bNNNNN), published several times a day. The semver release the GitHub API reports as 'latest' (v0.6.0) carries only nightly-tag.txt, no binaries, so a rolling build is the correct and only official binary source.
why_this_build: The reserve region's GPU image is runpod/pytorch:1.0.2-cu1281-torch280-ubuntu2404 with minCudaVersion 12.8, so the CUDA 12.8 x64 build matches the container exactly. The region's primary volume holds no llama.cpp and US-TX-3 has no capacity to read one from, so the reserve gets its own reproducible runtime instead of a byte copy of an unreachable binary.

verified_in_image.method: the trusted CI job llama-runtime-image pulls the image, mounts the staged runtime at /runtime and runs scripts/probe-runtime-in-image.sh inside it
verified_in_image.evidence: Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS, glibc 2.39, /usr/local/cuda-12.8/; libgomp.so.1 present (352304 bytes); ldd llama-server reports nothing missing; ldd libggml-cuda.so misses only libcuda.so.1, the driver the NVIDIA runtime supplies at real GPU start; llama-server --version reports 'version: 0.6.0-dev (build 11565, commit f9a95aeb2)'; --help lists every contract flag.
verified_in_image.why_it_matters: A bare ubuntu:24.04 image has no libgomp.so.1, which this build needs — that was the one gap a CPU Pod found. The production image provides it, so the reserve runtime needs no extra library and stays exactly the pinned official release.

provenance.note: Every release asset carries GitHub's own published sha256 digest. The pins below repeat that digest and scripts/verify-llama-runtime-pin.py re-reads the release and refuses any drift. Recomputing the digest of a downloaded file is a corruption check, not the provenance: the provenance is the digest the official release publishes.
provenance.commit_cross_check: The published binaries report 'build 11565, commit f9a95aeb2' from llama-server --version, which matches this pin's tag and commit.

bin.name: llama-b11565-bin-ubuntu-cuda-12.8-x64.tar.gz
bin.stages: the whole build directory, flat: llama-server, every lib*.so* (via its relative symlinks) and LICENSE

cudart.name: cudart-llama-b11565-bin-ubuntu-cuda-12.8-x64.tar.gz
cudart.why: The CUDA runtime libraries the GPU backend links against. The container image already provides them, so staging them next to the binary is defence in depth: with RUNPATH=$ORIGIN the staged pair loads on any host, which is exactly what a GPU-less CI runner proves.

contract.compatibility_note: Checked against common/arg.cpp at this exact commit: --n-gpu-layers takes N, 'auto' or 'all' (all -> -2), --flash-attn takes on|off|auto, and --ctx-size/--parallel/--alias/--jinja/--host/--port are unchanged. The existing start-llm.sh needs no edit.
